result.summary:
Independently re-derived from docs/agents/design/REQ-024.md itself (not CODE-DESIGNER's step-01-code-designer.json result.summary), against the live requirement text (docs/agents/requirements.yaml lines 1235-1263), the live schema (apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts), the live withdraw.ts/registration.ts/eventAuthorization.ts code, and the installed grammY package's actual InputFile type.

1. ZERO IMPLEMENTATION CODE (exhaustive). `grep -n '```'` finds 4 fenced pairs: lines 110-127 (MyRegistrationListItem interface + bare `getMyRegistrations(...): Promise<...>` signature, no body), 160-167 (CheckInQrInput interface + bare `renderCheckInQrPng(...): Promise<Buffer>` signature, no body), 216-218 (bare `makeMyCommandHandler(db): ...` signature, no body), 283-293 (Catalog.my interface, three `string;` fields with trailing comments, no bodies). None contains an if/return/arithmetic/comparison statement. All branching (the QR gate in Sec3 step 5f, the withdraw-button-eligibility gate in Sec0.2, the empty-vs-non-empty list branch in Sec3 steps 4-5) is stated in prose only ('if and only if admission==="admitted" and qrToken!==null', 'the button is shown iff the result's kind is "withdrawn"') -- exactly the discipline .claude/agents/code-designer.md requires after the REQ-016/017 traps, and the same style REQ-020/021/022/023 already passed with. The Sec2 template composition ('literal prefix / botUsername / literal / qrToken' as a table) is explicitly called out in the design's own text as deliberately not code, and it is correct that it isn't -- no operator, no concatenation syntax, just a table of literal pieces.

2. TOKEN REFERENCES. `grep -n 'var(--\|--color\|--space\|--font'` against the design file returns zero matches -- bot/backend requirement, no rendered UI, consistent with REQ-017/018/020/021/022/023 precedent (Sec header explicitly states 'No design tokens apply'). Nothing to check against tokens.css; correctly stated as N/A rather than silently skipped.

3. QRCODE DEPENDENCY CHOICE -- VERIFIED SOUND. Checked apps/bot/package.json directly: dependencies are exactly grammy/drizzle-orm/pg today, no QR library -- design's premise is accurate. No docs/agents/decisions/ record restricts adding a new npm dependency; 0004 (grammy) and 0005 (drizzle-orm/drizzle-kit) are the project's only precedent for adding a dependency via a WF-02 run, and both establish 'add to apps/bot/package.json, pin an exact version' as the norm -- the design recommends adding qrcode but does not itself state a pinned version number for BACKEND-DEV to use. This is a gap relative to the 0004/0005 precedent, but not a Step-1b blocking defect: pinning the exact installed version is BACKEND-DEV's own Step-2 mechanical action (npm install records the resolved version in package-lock.json regardless), not a design element an AC depends on -- filed as a MINOR non-blocking note, same category as REQ-023's carried MINOR issues.
   InputFile compatibility claim VERIFIED against the actually-installed package: read node_modules/grammy/out/types.node.d.ts lines 21-38 directly -- `InputFile`'s constructor accepts `MaybeSupplier<string | URL | URLLike | Uint8Array | ReadStream | ...>`; a Node `Buffer` is a `Uint8Array` subclass, so `qrcode`'s `toBuffer` return value (a plain `Buffer`) is directly and genuinely assignable to `new InputFile(buffer)` with no wrapping/conversion needed -- the design's claim is not merely plausible, it is confirmed against the live type definition.
   No native-binary/build-step claim: `qrcode` is a well-known pure-JS package (no node-gyp/native addon in its dependency tree); consistent with the design's own stated reasoning. Not independently re-verified via a live install (network fetch is out of scope for this gate), but the design's own reasoning is internally consistent and matches well-established public knowledge of the package, and BACKEND-DEV's Step 2 `npm install`+build will catch it immediately if wrong.

4. S3 STRUCTURAL-IMPOSSIBILITY CLAIM -- VERIFIED PRECISELY. Sec1's exact signature is `getMyRegistrations(db: DbClient["db"], userId: string): Promise<MyRegistrationListItem[]>` -- exactly one caller-derived parameter (userId), no eventId/registrationId/second-user-id anywhere in the parameter list, so there is no argument slot through which a second user's id could enter the WHERE clause even by a future maintainer's mistake. Traced handlers/my.ts's call chain per Sec3 steps 1-3: tgId resolved from ctx.from.id (Telegram's own authenticated sender id) -> actingUser resolved via resolveActingUser(db, BigInt(tgId)) (verified this function exists at domain/eventAuthorization.ts:28, the same function every other mutation/read handler already uses) -> getMyRegistrations(db, actingUser.id) is the only call, with actingUser.id sourced from step 2's output alone. No callback_data, message-text argument, or command argument is read anywhere in this path for user identity. Per-row rendering (Sec3 step 5) reads only fields already present on that same row (the row's own eventTitle/admission/qrToken/etc via the single join in Sec1) -- no second per-row lookup by any caller-suppliable id exists anywhere downstream, so no indirect leak path either. Structural claim holds.

5. AC3 (QR DECODABILITY) -- VERIFIED GENUINELY TESTABLE AS WORDED. renderCheckInQrPng composes the exact literal template `https://t.me/<botUsername>?start=ci_<qrToken>` and passes it to `qrcode`'s real PNG-buffer QR encoder (QRCode.toBuffer(text, {type:"png"})) -- qrcode is a standards-compliant QR (ISO/IEC 18004) encoder, so its output PNG is a genuine, scannable QR code decodable by any real QR decoder library (e.g. jsQR, a barcode-scanner CLI, or a physical phone camera) -- not a fake/placeholder image. This means AC3's literal wording ('decoded by an actual QR decoder... verified by decoding the produced image, not by inspecting the string passed to the encoder') is satisfiable exactly as stated: TEST-DESIGNER can write a test that runs a real decoder library against the produced Buffer and asserts the decoded string equals the exact composed template, with no need to fall back to string-inspection as a proxy. Flagging this positively for TEST-DESIGNER: this is a genuinely strong, non-circular AC given the chosen library, not a case where the design accidentally makes literal-wording compliance infeasible.

6. AC5 (SINGLE SHARED FUNCTION) -- VERIFIED GENUINELY STANDALONE. domain/qr.ts is a new, separate module from domain/registration.ts, explicitly framework-free (no grammy import per decisions/0004's discipline) and db-free (no DbClient parameter anywhere in CheckInQrInput or the function signature) -- its only inputs are botUsername and qrToken, both plain strings supplied by the caller. This means REQ-026's future T-3h reminder handler can import and call the exact same export with its own botUsername/qrToken values with zero duplication and zero coupling to /my's handler or database access pattern -- genuinely reusable, not something REQ-026 would need to fork or wrap. The design also explicitly names why the InputFile-wrapping stays in the handler (keeping domain/qr.ts framework-free), which is the correct place to draw that boundary for a second caller.

7. WITHDRAW-BUTTON REUSE -- VERIFIED ZERO CHANGE TO withdraw.ts, NO REGRESSION RISK. Read apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.ts directly: WITHDRAW_CONFIRM_PATTERN (line 21) and makeWithdrawConfirmCallbackHandler (line 103) already exist exactly as the design describes, keyed off callback_data matching `^withdraw:confirm:(.+)$`. The design's own callback button text (Sec3 step 5e) constructs callback_data as `withdraw:confirm:<registrationId>` -- the identical string shape this existing regex already matches -- and the design makes no edit to withdraw.ts anywhere in its text (grep of the design file for 'withdraw.ts' finds it only ever referenced as an unchanged dependency, never as a file this requirement modifies). Since REQ-022's own already-gated security/concurrency properties (the FOR UPDATE row lock, the ownerUserId===actingUserId check inside decideWithdrawOutcome) live entirely inside withdraw.ts/registration.ts and are untouched by this design, there is no mechanism by which this requirement could regress them -- /my's handler only ever emits a callback_data string that funnels into the exact same, unmodified handler REQ-022 already passed Step 2c for.

8. AC-TO-DESIGN-ELEMENT MAP -- re-derived against the live requirement text (requirements.yaml lines 1257-1262), not trusted from Sec6's own table. AC1 (user A sees only own rows) -> item 4 above. AC2 (live waitlist position, no write to viewer's row) -> Sec1/Sec3 step 5c: getWaitlistPosition (REQ-021, reused unchanged, verified present at registration.ts:266) recomputes fresh on every call; getMyRegistrations issues only a SELECT, no write. AC3 (QR decodes to exact deep link) -> item 5 above. AC4 (waitlisted/withdrawn/rejected show no QR) -> Sec3 step 5f's gate, `admission==="admitted" && qrToken!==null` stated in prose as the sole condition under which renderCheckInQrPng is even called; every other admission value falls through to plain ctx.reply, verified this is an exhaustive AdmissionState partition (schema.ts's qr_token column and the five-state enum already confirmed present). AC5 (single shared function) -> item 6 above. All 5 map to concrete, non-deferred design elements; Sec5's three open questions (pagination, ci_ deep-link decoding at check-in, per-row send-failure UX) are each explicitly named with an owner or explicit non-goal, never a silent gap in an AC-relevant area.

Verdict: PASS. No check failed.

issues.description: docs/agents/design/REQ-024.md Sec0.1 recommends adding the `qrcode` npm package but does not state a pinned exact version, whereas decisions/0004 and 0005 (the project's only two prior instances of adding a dependency) both establish 'pin an exact version' as the norm when a new dependency is introduced. Not blocking Step 1b: the version pin is a mechanical Step-2 action (BACKEND-DEV runs npm install and records the resolved version in package.json/package-lock.json), not a design element any acceptance criterion depends on. Recommend BACKEND-DEV pin the exact resolved version in apps/bot/package.json when implementing, matching the 0004/0005 convention, and REVIEWER check for it at Step 2b.
